full_judgment: 13. The learned court of appeal in the impugned judgment took a view that pendency of a partition suit amongst co-sharers is an impediment to grant temporary injunction in favour of the applicant. The manner of consideration for granting or rejecting a temporary injunction is the presumption of possession, not the pendency of any suit. If the applicant is found in exclusive possession of any land, temporary injunction can be allowed and pendency of any other suit in any form regarding the suit land is quite immaterial. It is now a laid down principle that if a co-sharer is found in exclusive possession of the suit land and the other co-sharers threatens the plaintiff from dispossessing from that exclusive possession, the person seeking temporary injunction should be protected till finality of the suit. The learned Counsel for the plaintiffs-respondents-petitioners referred to the decision laid down in the case of Ashek Ali Prodhania vs Md.
